en: At dawn, I remember her lovely lotus-face,
with its bimba-fruit-like lower lip and a nose graced by large pearls; her eyes reaching to her ears, adorned with jeweled earrings.
With a gentle smile, his forehead was radiant with the application of musk.
At dawn, I worship Lalitā’s wish-fulfilling vine of an arm, rich with sprout-like fingers shimmering with red rings,
and resplendent with ruby and golden bracelets and armlets.
Holding a lotus, a sugarcane bow, a flower-arrow, and a goad.
At dawn, I bow to the lotus-feet of Lalitā, which are intent on granting the desires of her devotees, which serve as a boat across the ocean of worldly existence,
and which are worthy of worship by the leaders of the gods, such as those seated upon the lotus-throne.
It is enriched with the emblems of the lotus, the goad, the banner, and the Sudarśana discus.
At dawn, I praise the supremely auspicious Lalitā Bhavānī, whose glory is known through the three Vedas, who is blameless in her compassion,
and who is the cause of the creation, dissolution, and maintenance of the universe.
The Sovereign of Knowledge, who is beyond the reach of the Vedas, speech, and mind.
In the morning, O Lalitā, I utter your auspicious names: Kāmeśvarī, Kamalā, Maheśvarī,
Śrī-Śāmbhavī, and Parā, the Mother of the worlds.
By the word "Vāgdevatā" [she is praised], and by the word "Tripureśvarī. ||5||
To whoever recites these five verses of Lalitāmbikā, which bestow good fortune and are most beautiful, at dawn,
Lalitā, being instantly pleased, grants her grace.
Knowledge, prosperity, stainless happiness, and infinite fame.
